title: Veined marble
purpose: Generate tileable PBR maps of polished or honed marble with long branching veins, soft clouds and fine secondary veins. Use for floors, counters, wall cladding and sculpture bases.

contract.signature: generate(width=256, height=256, seed=0, preset="default", directx_normal=False, **parameters) -> {map name: {"channels", "colour_space", "pixels"}}
contract.command_line: python marble_veined.py --size 1024 --seed 7 --preset NAME --out DIR [--width W --height H] [--set NAME=VALUE] [--directx-normal] [--orm]

parameters.name: vein_spacing
parameters.meaning: Noise cells across the veins: higher values give more, closer veins.

parameters.name: vein_direction
parameters.meaning: Vein run: 0 falling diagonal, 1 rising diagonal, 2 horizontal, 3 vertical, 4 steep diagonal.

parameters.name: vein_width
parameters.meaning: Average width of the main veins in texture units.

parameters.name: flow
parameters.meaning: Domain warp in texture units: how much the veins meander.

parameters.name: secondary_veins
parameters.meaning: Strength of the thin secondary veins.

parameters.name: cloudiness
parameters.meaning: Soft tonal clouds in the stone between veins.

parameters.name: polish
parameters.meaning: Surface finish from honed (0, matte) to polished (1, glossy).

parameters.name: hue_shift
parameters.meaning: Hue rotation of the albedo in turns.

presets.name: default
presets.description: White stone with soft grey diagonal veins, polished.

presets.name: calacatta
presets.description: Warm white stone with bold, widely spaced grey and gold veins.

presets.name: nero
presets.description: Black stone with sharp white veins.

presets.name: verde
presets.description: Dark green serpentine marble with pale meandering veins, honed.

presets.name: rosso
presets.description: Red-brown marble with cream veins and strong clouds.

limits: Veins are zero crossings of warped anisotropic noise, an approximation of mineral-filled fractures, not a geological simulation; vein directions are limited to five whole-tile shears so the texture repeats. Relief is very shallow by design. Colours are artistic, not measured from named quarries. Occlusion is a blurred-height estimate.
technique_references: Zero crossings of anisotropic fractional Brownian motion as vein curves
Distance to an isoline from the field gradient for constant-width lines
Domain warping with tileable gradient noise
Whole-tile shear as a torus automorphism
Height to tangent-space normal by central differences
